The only excuse offered is the driver's own written assertion that this was "for her own safety" and that she tried to open the door at the lights (F6); he offers no record of a dangerous act, and the GPS shows the car simply continued 15.4 km to Bedok Mall (F1), so the passenger was kept in the vehicle for the remainder of the trip after asking to leave at about 17:09.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is a narrative with no independent safety record; the driver's statement (F6) offers a safety justification ("tried to open the door at the lights"), and no fact in the table records what the rider did physically, so the judge may read F6 as a protective rather than threatening act.

No traffic/incident facts exist for this case, so the driver cannot be shown to have had a route-based reason to keep driving; equally, I have no system record beyond the chat timestamps (F3-F5) to show the rider was distressed at the time or asked a second time.

events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
WHAT HAPPENED. A RydeX trip Clarke Quay → Bedok Mall, pickup 17:08, drop-off 17:31, fixed fare $32.86. At 17:09 the rider messaged "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]; at 17:10 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F5], so the two messages are the whole exchange. The driver's written statement, made after the trip and not part of the chat, adds "The rider tried to open the door at the lights. I told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on." [F6]. The rider's complaint is that the driver threatened to lock her in and that she felt unsafe for the whole ride.

WHAT IS DISPUTED. The meaning of F4 read with F3 — a request to be let out immediately followed by a conditional "or I lock the doors" — is contested: the rider reads it as a threat/intimidation of a passenger who asked to leave a moving vehicle; the driver reads it as a safety instruction tied to the rider attempting to open a door [F3][F4][F6]. This is exactly the kind of semantic judgement SAFE-1 reserves to a human reading: the system must screen, not auto-decide, and the screen here is engaged [SAFE-1].

SAFETY SCREEN. I read every chat message, the complaint and the driver's statement. The complaint alleges being kept in the car ("threatened to lock me in ... felt unsafe for the whole ride"), and F4 is on its words a confinement ultimatum aimed at the rider right after she asked to alight [F3][F4][F6]. Given the asymmetric screen — a missed threat that lets a case auto-execute is not acceptable, and a false "suspected" merely costs a human look — I record this as "suspected" and decline to rule [SAFE-1]. The record also carries a detention-of-passenger / unsafe-ride allegation, which falls to the human reviewer under the safety-incident branch [SAFE-2].

WHY NO MONEY MOVES. The dispute is a safety incident, and the trace settles that a safety complaint permits only escalation. Independently, there is nothing to refund: actual distance 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (-0.1 km) [F1], duration +1.9 min [F2], and the fare is a fixed RydeX quote of $32.86, so under the non-metered branch no mileage-driven excess arises and no refund formula is available [RD-1][RD-2]; the rider's stop request [F3] was never agreed by the rider-side counterpart and no change-of-destination charge was added, so nothing to waive there either [FARE-1]. Amount is therefore null.

WHAT THE REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK: (1) whether F4, in context, is intimidation/abuse of a passenger rather than a safety instruction, and whether F6's safety gloss can be reconciled with the car continuing to Bedok Mall (F1); (2) the rider's account of what happened between 17:10 and drop-off, since the chat shows no further message from either party [F5] and F1/F2 say nothing about whether the car was stopped or moving at 17:09; (3) whether the rider attempted to open a door while moving, which F6 asserts but no gps/timeline fact records. Note the driver's profile (893 d, 4.62, 1038 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld) [F8] and the rider's clean profile [F7] are background only and do not decide this case [RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Refer the file to a human reviewer with the factual summary below; the reviewer should read F3 and F4 in context against F6, obtain the rider's full account of the remaining ride (17:10–17:31) via RydeHELP, and decide whether SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 action (and any account action) is warranted.

claims.assertion: The rider asked to be let out mid-trip: at 17:09 she messaged "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." (F3), a clear request to end her carriage and leave the vehicle.

The driver's reply at 17:10 was "Sit down or I lock the doors." (F4) — a conditional threat to confine the passenger in the car, made in response to her request to get out; on its words this is intimidation and a threat to her liberty of movement, not a safety instruction.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (F5), so the threat at F4 is not an artefact of missing or unreadable messages; the driver's later written statement (F6) does not deny it, it admits he "told her to sit down ... and drove on" after she tried to open the door.

The only excuse offered is the driver's own written assertion that this was "for her own safety" and that she tried to open the door at the lights (F6); he offers no record of a dangerous act, and the GPS shows the car simply continued 15.4 km to Bedok Mall (F1), so the passenger was kept in the vehicle for the remainder of the trip after asking to leave at about 17:09.

Ryde's Code of Conduct states that threats and intimidation of any kind will not be tolerated and that drivers must not take matters into their own hands but follow the reporting procedures (SAFE-1); the driver instead took matters into his own hands by refusing to stop and threatening to lock the doors (F4, F6), so the case must go to a person rather than be auto-decided.

The case involves the rider's own account of feeling unsafe and being kept in a moving vehicle for the whole ride after asking to get out (F3, F4), which is a safety incident requiring human handling and the RydeHELP report route rather than an automated fare ruling.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is a narrative with no independent safety record; the driver's statement (F6) offers a safety justification ("tried to open the door at the lights"), and no fact in the table records what the rider did physically, so the judge may read F6 as a protective rather than threatening act.

There is no route or fare irregularity to support the case: GPS shows actual distance 15.4 km vs optimal 15.5 km (-0.1 km) (F1) and the fare is a fixed RydeX quote, and no fare facts exist for this dispute type, so I cannot request any monetary refund — the outcome is necessarily escalation only.

The driver's profile (F8) shows 893 days, 4.62 rating, 1038 trips and zero disputes/zero upheld in 90 days, which the other side will use to argue this is out of character; the rider's clean profile (F7) does not corroborate her account either.

No traffic/incident facts exist for this case, so the driver cannot be shown to have had a route-based reason to keep driving; equally, I have no system record beyond the chat timestamps (F3-F5) to show the rider was distressed at the time or asked a second time.

claims.assertion: The record contains no safety-escalation trigger against the driver other than the rider's own complaint: the driver's only chat message is a safety instruction, F4 'Sit down or I lock the doors.', with no threat, insult, sexual advance or harassment in it, so nothing in the record meets the threshold in SAFE-1.

The driver's account of the same moment, F6 'The rider tried to open the door at the lights. I told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on.', is consistent with F4 and with a moving car at traffic lights; the rider's framing of F4 as a threat is her interpretation, not an independent record.

There is no route or fare grievance to correct: F1 shows the trip covered 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (-0.1 km, -0%), and F2 shows only +1.9 min over estimate, so no extra distance or charge was generated.

The rider's stop request came mid-journey at 17:09 (F3 'Please stop the car, I want to get out here.') and was never agreed by the driver, so no deviation, drop-off change or added stop was consented to, and no $3.00 change-of-destination charge could arise; the fare was the fixed RydeX quote.

The chat record is complete — F5 shows 2 messages, every one timestamped — so there is no evidentiary gap requiring human referral and no basis to fill in any words the complainant attributes to the driver.
The driver's account shows no pattern of misconduct: F8 records 2.4 years on the platform, rating 4.62, 1038 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes and 0 upheld, so no account flag is warranted under RD-6.

weaknesses: F4 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' is a directive about locking the rider in a moving vehicle; on its face it reads as detention, and the judge may treat it as an intimidation statement under SAFE-1 irrespective of the driver's safety motive in F6.

If the judge instead credits the rider's complaint as an allegation of dangerous driving or detention of a passenger, the case goes to a person under SAFE-2 on the strength of F3+F4 alone and no defence of mine can substitute for a factual finding on what happened in the car.

F1/F2 are GPS facts about distance and duration only; they say nothing about whether the car was moving when the rider asked to get out (F3), so they do not corroborate the driver's version in F6 about the lights.

The rider profile F7 shows a long-standing account (619 d, rating 4.8) with no dispute history, so the judge is unlikely to discount her account as self-serving, and my client has no independent witness to the exchange.

points.response: SAFE-1 is a screening duty, not a keyword list: the judge must read the record on every case, and the driver's own message 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' (F4) — a conditional threat to lock a passenger in a moving car immediately after she asked to get out (F3) — is exactly the kind of intimidation the judge, not the code, is to characterise; the driver's brief does not dispute the words of F4, only their characterisation.

F6 is the driver's own written statement made after the trip and so proves only what he asserts, whereas F4 is the contemporaneous message at 17:10 and F3 the contemporaneous request at 17:09; the system's rule that records beat statements means the words of F4, not the safety gloss in F6, govern — and F1 and F2 say nothing about whether the car was stopped at lights when the rider asked to be let out.

Conceded: F1 (-0.1 km) and F2 (+1.9 min) show no excess distance or charge, so my case is not a route or fare grievance and I seek no refund; the escalation rests solely on the safety exchange in F3/F4.

A complete, timestamped chat record (F5) is what makes the threat finding possible — it fixes F4 at 17:10, one minute after F3 — and completeness cuts against the driver, not for him; my escalation is for human assessment of that exchange, not for any evidentiary gap.

points.response: I do not ask for flag_account and agree the driver's profile (F8) shows no dispute pattern, so RD-6 is not engaged; profile facts cannot decide this case either way, and the safety question stands on F4 itself.

Accepted as far as it goes: F3 shows a mid-trip request to stop, but a request is not an agreement and no clause converts it into a right the driver must satisfy instantly; the rider's remedy was to escalate with Ryde, not to open the door of a moving car.

F4 is one sentence whose meaning is genuinely contested, and the advocate's reading of it as a threat is an interpretation, not something the text establishes; F6 places the words in a safety context, and F1 confirms the car was on a normal 15.4 km run, not a confinement.

The record's completeness (F5) cuts both ways: it means the judge reads exactly two messages, one of which is my client's order to sit down; there is no second demand from the rider and no further message from the driver, so nothing in the record shows any continued threat during the remaining 20-odd minutes of the trip.

F6 does not admit confinement — it says the rider tried to open the door at the lights and the driver told her to sit down and drove on; F1 shows the trip ended where it was supposed to (15.4 km, effectively the 15.5 km optimal), so there is no record of the driver taking the rider anywhere but Bedok Mall or of any additional charge.

SAFE-1 lists threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual harassment and personal abuse; the record contains no such words, only a safety instruction (F4) which the driver's statement ties to an attempt to open the door in a moving car (F6), so the fact that the case is escalated for human reading is not a finding against my client.

Notwithstanding my client's denial of the rider's version, the rider's own complaint that she felt unsafe for the whole ride is itself a safety allegation, so the record is properly referred to a person under SAFE-2 and my client will cooperate with that review; a human reader should weigh F4 and F6 together, not F4 alone.

I keep D2: F6 is the only system-side account of the physical moment, and the rider's complaint supplies no competing record of what she did in the car, so the judge has F4+F6 against a narrative alone.

I keep D6 as a plea against any account action: F8 shows 2.4 years, 4.62 rating, 1038 trips and 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days, and nothing in F1–F6 shows a completed trip charged without the rider aboard or any other listed violation.
